 Indigenous AI Foundation Models
 Star marking (1-5) indicates the importance of topic for CSE -->
 19 Nov 2026 
 8 min read
 Tags: Quick Facts For Prelims 
 GS Paper - 3 
 GS Paper - 2 
 Artificial Intelligence 
 Government Policies & Interventions 
 Source: IE   
 Why in News?    
 The IndiaAI Mission under the Union Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) launched three indigenous foundation language models : EKA-1 , Dhir 2B , and Dhir 5B .    
 Developed by Indian startups under the IndiaAI Innovation Centre (Foundation Models) pillar, with subsidised access to national AI compute infrastructure, these models advance the vision of “Make AI in India and Make AI Work for India.”     
 What are the Three Indigenous Foundation Language Models?   
 EKA-1   
 Developer: Soket Labs Technology and Research Private Limited (Soket AI Labs) under Project EKA.   
 Architecture & Scale: An open-source, sparse hybrid language model with 26.3 billion parameters , trained on roughly 7.5 trillion tokens .    
 Its "sparse" design activates only part of the model per task, conserving computing power.   
 Language Coverage: Supports all 22 scheduled Indian languages and English.   
 Core Applications: Built for complex tasks including mathematics, coding, reasoning, and agentic AI (multi-step task execution), with a strong focus on BFSI (Banking, Financial Services, and Insurance) and cybersecurity .   
 Dhir 2B and Dhir 5B   
 Developer: ZenteiQ AiTech Innovations , a Bengaluru-based AI startup.   
 Architecture & Scale: Open-source, lightweight Small Language Models (SLMs) with 2 billion and 5 billion parameters.   
 Language Coverage: Supports English and 10 Indian languages .   
 Offline & On-Premise Capability: Designed to run offline, on-premise, and on-device (including mobile phones) without cloud connectivity—keeping sensitive data local.   
 Core Applications: Document-grounded automation, knowledge retrieval, and citizen/enterprise services across defence, government, industry, and education , especially in low-connectivity or sensitive environments such as border areas.   
 Need for Indigenous Foundation Language Models   
 Strategic Autonomy & Sovereign AI: Reduces India’s dependence on foreign, predominantly Western AI systems for critical sectors like defence, governance, and financial services.   
 Data Security & Privacy: On-premise and on-device models (like Dhīr 2B and 5B) process information locally, ensuring sensitive national and citizen data never leaves domestic infrastructure.   
 Bridging the Linguistic Divide: Enables millions of non-English speakers to access digital services in healthcare, education, agriculture, and e-governance in their native tongues, complementing platforms like BHASHINI .   
 Eliminating the "Token Tax" via Native Indic Tokenisers: Commercial LLMs (such as GPT-4) rely on English-centric tokenisers that split Indic scripts into numerous subword and byte-level pieces, causing a sentence requiring 10 tokens in English to consume 35 to 140 tokens in an Indian language .    
 Since AI services charge per token, regional language processing becomes slow and expensive. Rich, culturally grounded regional datasets are essential to train native Indic tokenisers and eliminate this "token tax."    
 Last-Mile Access in Low-Connectivity Zones: Lightweight, offline-capable models allow AI tools to function reliably in rural, remote, and high-security zones without requiring high-speed internet.   
 Strengthen Indic Data Ecosystems: Develop high-quality, culturally representative datasets and efficient Indic tokenisers in collaboration with native speakers, universities and linguistic institutions.    
 Integrating  these resources with AIKosh , the IndiaAI Mission’s shared platform for datasets, AI models and development tools, to improve accessibility and promote indigenous AI innovation.

 Key Highlights & Focus Areas   
 BharatGen (Param 2 – 17B)   
 Government-supported consortium led by IIT Bombay (IndiaAI Mission)   
 Multilingual & Multimodal Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) LLM   
 Covers 22 scheduled Indian languages + English ; designed for public-sector, governance, education, and research applications.   
 Sarvam AI ( Sarvam 30B & 105B, Bulbul, Sarvam Vision )   
 Sarvam AI (backed under IndiaAI Mission)   
 Open-Source LLMs, Speech (ASR/TTS) & Vision AI   
 Trained for high-accuracy Indic language processing, document understanding, voice AI (Bulbul) and DPDP Act, 2023 -compliant enterprise workloads.   
 Gnani.ai   
 Gnani.ai (backed under IndiaAI Mission)   
 Speech-to-Speech & Conversational Voice AI   
 Focuses on Indian-language voice recognition, speech synthesis, and direct voice-to-voice interaction for digital assistants and enterprise conversations.   
 Krutrim   
 Ola AI   
 Multilingual LLM   
 Cloud-native Indian language model supporting English and 22 Indian languages for consumer, coding, mobility, and logistics use cases.   
 Varya AI   
 Avataar AI (backed under IndiaAI Mission)   
 Video Generation Model   
 Indigenous AI video generation model launched in June 2026 for visual and media content creation.   
 Project Indus   
 Tech Mahindra (IndiaAI Mission team)   
 Indic LLM   
 Enterprise-oriented foundation language model tailored for Indian-language understanding and vernacular applications.   
 Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)   
 1. What are the three indigenous foundation language models launched under the IndiaAI Mission?
 The three models are EKA-1 , developed by Soket AI Labs, and Dhir 2B and Dhir 5B , developed by Bengaluru-based ZenteiQ AiTech Innovations.   
 2. What is the IndiaAI Mission, and which ministry implements it?
 The IndiaAI Mission is a national initiative approved in 2024 to build a robust AI ecosystem through compute infrastructure, indigenous AI development, datasets, skilling and responsible AI. It is implemented by the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) .   
 3. What is the 'Token Tax' in multilingual AI systems?
 It refers to the higher token consumption and associated computational costs when English-centric tokenisers process Indian languages. Native Indic tokenisers can improve linguistic efficiency and reduce processing costs.   
 UPSC Civil Services Examination Previous Year Question 
 Prelims     
 Q. With the present state of development, Artificial Intelligence can effectively do which of the following? (2020) 
 Bring down electricity consumption in industrial units        
 Create meaningful short stories and songs        
 Disease diagnosis        
 Text-to-Speech Conversion        
 Wireless transmission of electrical energy        
 Select the correct answer using the code given below:   
 (a) 1, 2, 3 and 5 only    
 (b) 1, 3 and 4 only    
 (c) 2, 4 and 5 only    
 (d) 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5   
 Ans: (b)
